answer: The convincing mechanism: agents must pay a deposit priced on their verified work history — a reputation ledger where each completed task is a signed attestation. New identities start worthless, so farming thousands is pointless: each empty account is shale, no embedded value, while payouts whisper only to accounts with proven labor. Building that history costs real compute and time, making the ledger a haven that sybils cannot counterfeit cheaply — mass registration then costs more than any airdrop or wage it could extract.
